races.name: BetGoodwin Download The App Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Lola De Magny
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the race shape but needs to prove she can handle this extended trip having raced over shorter distances recently.
runners_data.comment: No threat when 3rd on both hurdle runs but this point winner could go well on h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't threatened when third this year on her first two starts over hurdles (2m4f, soft/good to soft) but this 3m point winner now goes handicapping off a realistic mark and could be suited by the step up in trip.

runners_data.name: All Authorized
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner now 10lb lower than his last win, with the Moores' stable in decent form and the longer trip potentially suiting.
runners_data.comment: Disappointing season but now 10lb lower than when winning over C&D last April
runners_data.spotlight: He's had a disappointing season, initially over fences and more recently over hurdles, and has something to prove; however, he's now 10lb lower than when winning over C&D (good) last April and can't be written off; monitor the betting.

runners_data.name: The Wise Traveller
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner returning from 95-day break with previous good record when fresh, but three consecutive seventh-place finishes are concerning.
runners_data.comment: Below par when last seen but break may have helped; C&D win off 3lb higher last September
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who has finished merely seventh on his last three starts, the latest in January; however, a break may have helped and he was returning from some time off when winning under Jamie Gambin over C&D (good) last September; now 3lb lower than for that win and not discounted.

runners_data.name: Hilltown
runners_data.note: Hold-up style fits but has struggled badly this season and carries headgear changes indicating ongoing issues.
runners_data.comment: Two-time course winner but he's struggled this season (including here) after long absence
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D in April 2023 and a chase here in April 2024; however, he's struggled this season following a long absence, including at this course on three occasions; 4lb out of the handicap; major turnaround needed.

runners_data.name: Local Derby
runners_data.note: Point winner over 3m whose hold-up style perfectly suits this race shape, recent Wincanton success shows he's in form.
runners_data.comment: Progressive 6yo who has won his last two completed starts and holds leading claims
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground 3m point winner who scored at Wincanton (2m4f, heavy) in January on second handicap start, and after an early unseat at Fontwell (jumped path) he returned to winning ways at Exeter (2m7f, good to soft) three weeks ago; this progressive 6yo has leading claims up 6lb for last time.

runners_data.name: Mild Magic
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who showed promise when third at this course in February but generally struggles to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: Step in right direction here last time and the longer trip/better ground may help today
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't been able to get seriously competitive across her five rules runs, in handicaps on last two occasions, but at least her 13l third here (2m4f, soft) in February was a step in the right direction; this 3m point runner-up (good to yielding) could build on it now up in trip and on better ground.

runners_data.name: Barrow Ranger
runners_data.note: Irish raider with hold-up style but poor recent rules form makes him hard to fancy despite point success.
runners_data.comment: Irish raider; hard to fancy on rules form but won a point two starts ago; watch the market
runners_data.spotlight: He's hard to fancy on his rules form and was soundly beaten over fences last time, but he won a point-to-point two starts ago and this 5yo Irish challenger is one to watch in the betting.

races.paceDynamic: The Wise Traveller stands alone as the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the start in this 3m1f contest. With six hold-up horses behind him including Local Derby, All Authorized, and Lola De Magny, the 10-year-old can establish a comfortable rhythm without early pressure. This creates a tactical race where stamina and finishing kick become paramount over 3+ miles on good ground. The race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can deliver late charges, as The Wise Traveller's uncontested lead will set up a finishing test that suits patient tactics.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller sets moderate fractions without pressure from the field.
scenarios.body: The lone leader creates perfect conditions for closers to unleash finishing kicks, with the extended trip favouring horses who can quicken late. Local Derby and All Authorized benefit most from this tactical setup given their proven stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller maintains honest fractions throughout the contest.
scenarios.body: A true test of stamina emerges where the best stayers prevail, suiting horses with proven form at the trip. This scenario particularly helps Local Derby who won his point over 3m and All Authorized with his staying credentials.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Surprises Field
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller's 95-day break has rejuvenated the 10-year-old.
scenarios.body: An uncontested lead allows the front-runner to steal crucial lengths, making it difficult for hold-up horses to close the gap. His previous good form when fresh makes this scenario viable despite recent poor runs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If The Wise Traveller stops quickly in the final furlong after leading throughout.
scenarios.body: A crawling pace becomes a sprint finish where horses with tactical speed matter most. This unlikely scenario would suit those who can quicken despite being positioned for stamina tests.

watchPoints.text: The Wise Traveller could steal the race if his 95-day break has refreshed him and he gets uncontested fractions.
Local Derby's jumping after his recent unseat at Fontwell could determine whether he can utilise his tactical advantage.
All Authorized's ability to recapture his best form now handicapped 10lb lower than his last victory.
How aggressively the hold-up horses position themselves if The Wise Traveller sets slow fractions.
Whether any of the hold-up brigade attempts to provide early pressure rather than all waiting to pounce.

races.name: BetGoodwin Sussex Champion Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Edwardstone
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suits the expected strong pace, though 51 days off and age 12 raise fitness questions.
runners_data.comment: 12yo who showed with Grade 2 win in January he retains considerable spark; leading player
runners_data.spotlight: 12yo whose career highlight came when winning the Tingle Creek in 2022; showed he retains considerable spark when winning Grade 2 at Kempton (2m4f, good) this January; he may prefer a longer trip than this nowadays but he's a leading player nevertheless now back in a handicap.

runners_data.name: Matterhorn
runners_data.note: Front-running style with 107 days since last run creates stamina doubts in this pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Won in good style at Uttoxeter last May; pulled up on sole run since but could bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 5-9 over fences with convincing win at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) last May; pulled up on sole run since, at Ascot in December, but the good to soft ground may not have suited; second in this last year; could go well.

runners_data.name: Kotmask
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who benefits from strong pace but jumping errors and poor recent Newbury form are major concerns.
runners_data.comment: Jumping issues this term but has good record here; may not be far away if finding fluency
runners_data.spotlight: His jumping has been an issue this season and he was soundly beaten at Newbury last time; however, two starts ago he was a close second of four there (2m, good to soft) and he has a good record at this track; might not be far away if finding some fluency.

runners_data.name: Secret Des Dieux
runners_data.note: Front-runner in good form but 7lb rise and having to battle two other pace-setters creates pressure.
runners_data.comment: 6yo novice; did it very nicely at Kempton last month to make it 3-6 over fences; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Capitalised on the drop back in trip to win at Huntingdon (2m, heavy) in February and followed up at Kempton (2m2f, good); he's 7lb higher than last time and in a hotter race, but did it very nicely and this 6yo novice is now 3-6 over fences; could still have more to offer and he's respected.

runners_data.name: Scorsese
runners_data.note: Another pace-setter whose Boxing Day win came in easier company, now faces stronger opposition while making the running.
runners_data.comment: In good form over 2m3f/2m4f; this trip could suit but he's 4lb wrong at the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Made all at Sedgefield (2m3f, good to soft) on Boxing Day on fourth chase start and his good form has continued when third on both runs since (2m4f, soft/good to soft); this drop back in trip is worth a go and further improvement is possible, but he needs to be better than ever from 4lb wrong.

races.paceDynamic: Matterhorn, Secret Des Dieux and Scorsese will ensure a strong gallop from the start over this stamina-testing 2m1f trip at Plumpton. With three confirmed front-runners in a small field, the pace will be honest throughout and likely turn into a battle of attrition up the hill. The relentless tempo will stretch the field and expose any fitness concerns, particularly over Plumpton's demanding undulations. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can conserve energy early and produce a sustained finish when the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too fast early and tie up over the demanding Plumpton hills.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will stretch them beyond their limits, allowing the hold-up horses to pick up the pieces with sustained finishes. Edwardstone and Kotmask benefit most from their patient tactics when the leaders fold.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters breaks clear and the others can't sustain the gallop.
scenarios.body: Secret Des Dieux looks the most progressive of the leaders and could dictate terms if Matterhorn and Scorsese fade. His recent Kempton win shows he can control the tempo and has the stamina for this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes more measured with the three leaders checking each other.
scenarios.body: A more sedate tempo would suit the front-runners' stamina reserves but reduce the setup for hold-up horses. This scenario is less likely given three confirmed pace-setters who prefer to lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If all three front-runners go off too fast and completely collapse in the straight.
scenarios.body: An extreme version where the early pace is suicidal, leaving just the hold-up horses to fight it out. Kotmask's fitness concerns after his poor Newbury run make this his best chance if it develops into a crawl home.

watchPoints.text: Matterhorn and Scorsese both return from breaks and may not handle the expected fierce pace battle.
Kotmask's jumping has been problematic this season and errors could prove costly in a small field.
Secret Des Dieux carries 7lb more than his last win and faces his toughest pace battle yet.
Edwardstone's 51-day break at age 12 needs monitoring for fitness in the closing stages.
The three front-runners will create an honest gallop that should set up perfectly for the hold-up horses.

races.name: Roy Reeve Memorial Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Oblemenko
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with unknown hurdle style but represents a stable with a good record in this specific race, making him hard to assess tactically
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten in both points; check market but others have more compelling credentials
runners_data.spotlight: Brother to bumper/hurdle winner Sansrick (RPR 121); soundly beaten in both Irish maiden points; one of two for stable that has good record in this race; market check advised but others have far more compelling credentials.

runners_data.name: Loriko
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with highest rating who needs the race to develop into a staying test to showcase his class advantage
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on handicap debut at Hereford but tough to beat if rediscovering earlier form
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten on handicap debut at Hereford (2m3f) in December when soft going shouldn't have been an issue (ran well on testing ground in France); however, he ran really well in defeat in the autumn on his first three British starts (2m-2m3f, good) and will be tough to beat if rediscovering that form.

runners_data.name: Flash Man
runners_data.note: Promising hold-up type who showed improvement last time at Kempton and could benefit from another step forward over hurdles
runners_data.comment: 2 Flat wins in France; 3rd at Kempton on second hurdle run; can give another good account
runners_data.spotlight: Two-time French Flat winner who was a promising third at Kempton (2m, good) a fortnight ago on his second hurdle start; open to further improvement in this code and can give another good account.

runners_data.name: Tetsworth
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner making his second hurdle start with the tactical advantage of dictating terms from the front
runners_data.comment: 0-8 on the Flat but with ability; encouraging fourth on sole hurdle start and can improve
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 on the Flat but has shown a fair level of ability in that code, including on last two starts; shaped when fourth of nine on hurdle debut at Kempton (2m, good) in December as though he would improve for that experience; stable has strong record in race; he could be the main threat to Loriko.

runners_data.name: Answer That
runners_data.note: Fellow pace-setter whose poor recent hurdle form suggests he may struggle to cope if the pace becomes truly testing
runners_data.comment: Showed promise in bumpers in Ireland but tailed off on first two hurdle starts
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise when making the frame in two bumpers in Ireland (soft to heavy/yielding); however, tailed off on his first two hurdle starts (2m, soft/good to soft) and needs to be an entirely different proposition today.

races.paceDynamic: Tetsworth and Answer That are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early pace in this small field, creating an honest gallop from the start. With only five runners, there's nowhere to hide and the two leaders will likely ensure a decent tempo throughout the 2m trip. Flash Man and Loriko are both hold-up horses who will need to be produced late, while Oblemenko's style is unclear but he's lightly raced. This pace scenario clearly favours the prominent racers and those with tactical speed, as the strong early gallop will set up the race for horses that can position close to the pace rather than those needing to come from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace Suits Class
scenarios.trigger: If both Tetsworth and Answer That go forward and maintain a solid gallop
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will find out the weaker horses and allow the classier performers like Loriko to close late with their superior ratings. Flash Man could also benefit from this setup given his recent Kempton promise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes more moderate with the leaders getting an easier time of it
scenarios.body: Tetsworth and Answer That can utilize their natural speed advantage and kick clear before the hold-up horses can respond. The small field means less pressure on the leaders throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners drops out early or they go too slow initially
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where Flash Man's recent Kempton form and Loriko's class can tell. However, this seems unlikely given both leaders' natural running styles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Mystery Horse Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Oblemenko shows significantly more ability than his Irish point form suggests
scenarios.body: The Moore stable's good record in this race could be significant and he might have been well-schooled at home. His lightly raced profile offers the most potential improvement.

watchPoints.text: Watch if both Tetsworth and Answer That go too fast early as this could set up the race perfectly for Loriko's late charge
Monitor Flash Man's jumping throughout as any mistakes could prove costly in a small field where every position matters
Observe how confidently Oblemenko travels in the early stages to gauge whether he's been primed for a breakthrough performance
Check if Answer That shows any early signs of struggling as his recent hurdle form suggests he may not handle a strong pace
Watch for Loriko's position turning in as he'll need to be close enough to strike when the race develops

races.name: Southern Cranes & Access Ltd Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Easy Love
runners_data.note: Front-running style suited Windsor success but 37 days off and Grade race failures on soft/heavy suggest vulnerability when pressed
runners_data.comment: Easily made all at Windsor in January on last handicap start and she's one to consider
runners_data.spotlight: Course bumper winner who easily made all on handicap debut at Windsor (2m4f, good) on New Year's Day; unplaced/pulled up in Grade 2/Listed races on heavy/soft going on her two starts since but she could be an entirely different proposition now back in a handicap and back on better ground.

runners_data.name: Religous Cross
runners_data.note: Hold-up style ideal but 63-day absence and poor Kempton effort raise fitness concerns despite Taunton win
runners_data.comment: Just four runs, with wins in a point/novice hurdle; unexposed and could have more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who scored on his hurdle debut at Taunton (2m3f, good) in December; 28l fourth of 15 in Kempton novice (2m5f, good to soft) since but this unexposed 6yo makes his handicap debut off what looks a fair mark and he could have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Maldini Milano
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with cheekpieces retained from C&D success but 78 days off is a worry for Nicholls yard
runners_data.comment: C&D maiden winner; weakened on handicap debut but on soft; firmly in calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground bumper winner who got off the mark over hurdles at the third attempt over C&D (good) in November, when wearing first-time cheekpieces (retained) in a maiden that worked out extremely well; weakened into sixth on handicap debut at Windsor in January but that was on soft ground; firmly in calculations now back on a better surface.

runners_data.name: Mount Anglesby
runners_data.note: Prominent style and progressive form for new yard makes him dangerous, only 29 days since last run keeps him sharp
runners_data.comment: Progressive for new yard this term and has won two of his last three starts; respected
runners_data.spotlight: 7yo who has a fair bit of experience but has been progressive for a new yard this term, making it two wins from his last three runs (2m3f/2m5f, good/good to soft) when scoring at Warwick last time; entitled to respect.

runners_data.name: The Boss Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with C&D win but pulled up twice recently suggests stamina/jumping issues over this trip
runners_data.comment: Won on hurdle debut over C&D in December but pulled up/well beaten in his two handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Won a bumper at Fontwell (2m1f, good) last May and followed up on hurdle debut over C&D (good to soft) in December; however, he's been pulled up/well beaten in his first two handicaps and needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Minella Jury
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was travelling well when falling last time, stamina proven but jumping reliability questioned
runners_data.comment: Disputing lead when final-flight faller at Doncaster and the winner followed up
runners_data.spotlight: Irish bumper winner (yielding) who followed up on hurdle/stable debut at Uttoxeter (2m, heavy) in December, and he was disputing the lead and clear of the rest when falling at the final flight on handicap debut at Doncaster (2m, good to soft) last time; the winner has followed up off 6lb higher so a 4lb rise for this fellow may well prove lenient; every chance he'll stay.

runners_data.name: Kel Du Large
runners_data.note: Front-runner with cheekpieces who was close second to Mount Anglesby last time but may lack tactical speed
runners_data.comment: Listed bumper winner for whom things are clicking over hurdles; possible contender
runners_data.spotlight: Listed bumper winner who scored at Hereford (2m3f, heavy) in February on his third handicap start and was a close second to Mount Anglesby (2m5f, good to soft) four weeks ago; this 6yo could continue to progress now things are starting to click; possible contender in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Tennessee Tango
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with tongue-tie but pulled up in handicap company last time after maiden success
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in competitive EBF Final at Sandown but progressive previously; not written off
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground bumper runner-up who improved with each of his first four runs over hurdles, easily winning a maiden here (2m, soft) in February; pulled up in the competitive EBF Final at Sandown (2m4f, soft) since and needs to prove his stamina, but pedigree provides hope; not written off.

runners_data.name: High Fibre
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in great form with recent Kempton win and Ludlow second, only 7 days between runs could be tight
runners_data.comment: Improved form last month, with a win and a near-miss; could again be thereabouts
runners_data.spotlight: Began to look exposed in the second half of last year but he showed improved form to win at Kempton (2m, good) on March 23 and was short-headed at Ludlow (2m, good) last Monday; he should be fine now back up in trip and could again be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Percy Shelley
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with useful flat form but 135-day absence is major concern despite quality performances when fresh
runners_data.comment: Useful on Flat; good start to hurdling career; pulled up last time but retains potential
runners_data.spotlight: Useful Flat performer who made good start to hurdling career in the autumn, including when going close in a Cheltenham novice (2m4f, good to soft; has won on good ground); flopped at Ascot (2m5f, good) in November but has had a break since and retains potential now in his first handicap hurdle.

runners_data.name: Jefe Triunfo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping in class but 147 days off and poor recent form makes him hard to recommend
runners_data.comment: Didn't show enough in handicaps in the autumn to have pressing claims today
runners_data.spotlight: Won a maiden hurdle at Warwick (2m, good) last June and has dropped down the weights, but he didn't show enough in handicaps in the autumn to have pressing claims today; returns from a break.

runners_data.name: Grand Conqueror
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with C&D win but all form on soft ground, making good ground debut a significant unknown
runners_data.comment: 2-2 in handicaps before coming clear with well-treated winner last time; lots to like
runners_data.spotlight: Won on handicap debut over C&D (good to soft) in December and followed up at Fontwell (2m1f, good to soft) 11 days later, before clear second to well-handicapped winner at Kempton (2m5f, good to soft) in February; he's up 4lb for last time but the form reads very well and he could settle better in a first-time hood; lots to like.

races.paceDynamic: Easy Love and Kel Du Large are the two confirmed front-runners who will contest the early pace, with Easy Love particularly keen to make all after his Windsor success. The honest gallop they set over this extended trip will create a searching test that should stretch the field out, preventing any sprint finish. Mount Anglesby and Tennessee Tango sitting prominent can track the pace without being embroiled in the early battle. This searching pace over 2m4½f strongly favours hold-up horses who can pick off tired leaders, as the early tempo will take its toll on those racing keenly up front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners Easy Love and Kel Du Large go too fast early and weaken
scenarios.body: The honest pace will stretch the field and allow patient riders on Percy Shelley, High Fibre and The Boss Bear to time their challenges perfectly. Those racing off the pace can exploit the tiring leaders over this stamina-sapping trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Mount Anglesby and Tennessee Tango get the perfect position tracking the pace without racing keenly
scenarios.body: They can strike when the leaders weaken but before the hold-up horses get organized. Their proven stamina over similar trips gives them the edge in a sustained drive from the home turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Easy Love gets an uncontested lead with Kel Du Large struggling to go the pace early
scenarios.body: Easy Love's Windsor form suggests he can sustain a strong gallop and his proven stamina over this trip may allow him to repel all challengers. The lack of early pressure would conserve enough energy for the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners are pulled up or fall early leaving no pace in the race
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy affair with no clear tempo, suiting horses who can quicken from any position. This tactical lottery could favour the most experienced or best-handicapped runners regardless of usual style.

watchPoints.text: Easy Love could get an uncontested lead if Kel Du Large doesn't jump off quickly enough, making the favourite very hard to catch
Percy Shelley's 135-day absence is extreme even for a hold-up horse, watch market confidence and early moves carefully
Tennessee Tango was pulled up in handicap company last time so monitor jumping and travelling throughout
Mount Anglesby and High Fibre both in great current form, watch which one gets the better position tracking the pace
Religous Cross and Grand Conqueror both absent 63 days for the same trainer, stable confidence indicators crucial

races.name: BetGoodwin Sussex National Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Transmission
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 64-day break with strong recent Musselburgh win, first-time visor clearly helped last time
runners_data.comment: Easily won the Edinburgh National at Musselburgh and an 8lb rise may not stop him
runners_data.spotlight: Tapped back into last season's promising form, and then some, to win by 12l in a first-time visor at Musselburgh (3m7f, good to soft; Edinburgh National) in February; has also won on good ground and 2-2 over hurdles here; an 8lb rise may not stop him if the visor maintains its positive effect.

runners_data.name: Largy Poet
runners_data.note: Front-runner back in cheekpieces after pulling up in blinkers, inconsistent but capable when right
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent and pulled up last time but back in cheekpieces today and he's not discounted
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent and pulled up in first-time blinkers at Exeter (3m6f, heavy) in February; however, he's back in cheekpieces today in which he kept on for second of six at Wincanton (3m1f, heavy) in January; versatile ground-wise and this sort of trip may yet suit; not discounted.

runners_data.name: Rivers Corner
runners_data.note: Front-runner in excellent form with recent Exeter win despite bad mistake, clearly on the upgrade
runners_data.comment: He's won two of his last three, most recently over 3m6f; clearly on the up
runners_data.spotlight: Easy win at Wincanton (3m2f, heavy) in January and bounced back from Haydock flop to win at Exeter (3m6f, good) recently, despite a bad mistake; clearly on the up and his stable has won two of the last six runnings.

runners_data.name: Invincible Nao
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has won this race before and thrives at Plumpton, strong course record
runners_data.comment: Won this last year and running well in the main this season; chance
runners_data.spotlight: Kicked off 2025 with two wins in a row here (3m1f/3m4f, soft), including this race, and he reappeared with another win at Sandown (2m4f, good) in November; has continued in good form since in the main; chance.

runners_data.name: Sea Invasion
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent course form, 51 days off but trainer strikes at low frequency

runners_data.name: Unanswered Prayers
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who hasn't threatened since Southern National win, dangerous mark but aged 10
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark on form as recent as October but this 10yo hasn't threatened since
runners_data.spotlight: Won the Southern National (3m3f, good) in November 2024 and he's on a dangerous mark on form as recent as October 2025; however, this 10yo hasn't threatened since and needs to raise his game.

runners_data.name: Planned Paradise
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with recent back-to-back wins, 12-day turnaround but in good form
runners_data.comment: Has won his last two starts in good style; up in the weights but clearly in rude health
runners_data.spotlight: Exploited a reduced mark to win at Bangor (3m5f, soft) in February and again had plenty in hand at Hexham (4m, soft) 12 days ago; this is a hotter race than last time and this 10yo is up 10lb, but he's clearly in rude health and could be bang there once more; handles any ground.

runners_data.name: Tommie Beau
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong Plumpton record but 72 days off and struggling on higher marks
runners_data.comment: Strong record here and has a reduced mark but this 11yo is hard to fancy on recent form
runners_data.spotlight: He's won here three times and was second in this race in 2024 on his last Plumpton visit; on a reduced mark but this 11yo has struggled to get competitive on his last few starts and needs to turn things around in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Stans The Man
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to form with recent Wincanton win, good record on similar going
runners_data.comment: Back to form to win at Wincanton last month and his revised mark may be within range
runners_data.spotlight: Won two in a row last May (3m5f/3m3f, good) and returned to form to win at Wincanton (3m1f, good to soft) last month following a break; this 9yo has never defied a mark this high but it may be within range if he's once more at the top of his game.

runners_data.name: Havaila
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with course and distance win last year, 16 days since convincing Windsor success
runners_data.comment: Convincing win at Newbury last month and this progressive 7yo has the necessary stamina
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D (good) last March and reappeared with creditable third of 16 at Windsor (3m4f, soft) in January; bounced back from lesser run with convincing win at Newbury (2m7f, good to soft) last month and this progressive 7yo may be able to take a 9lb rise in his stride.

runners_data.name: Enjoy d'Allen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with three small-field wins this season, big step up in class here
runners_data.comment: Three small-field wins this season; this 12yo may find today's race too competitive
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins in small fields this season (2m5f-3m5f, good/soft) and another good run when second of three at Sedgefield (3m2f, good) recently; however, there's a suspicion this 12yo will find today's race too competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Largy Poet and Rivers Corner are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early pace, creating an honest gallop from the outset over this extended trip. Rivers Corner comes here in excellent form with recent wins and will likely dictate terms, while Largy Poet brings inconsistency but strong pace pressing ability. The sustained early tempo will stretch the field and create opportunities for those who can stay strongly up the hill finish at Plumpton. This pace setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay the trip and finish with a wet sail.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Rivers Corner and Largy Poet go too hard early and fade from 2f out.
scenarios.body: The honest pace stretches stamina reserves and allows patient hold-up horses to sweep past the tiring pace-setters in the final half-mile. Transmission and Invincible Nao are perfectly positioned to benefit from this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Horse Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Rivers Corner gets an easy lead and controls the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Without sufficient early pressure, Rivers Corner can dictate terms and kick clear turning for home with plenty left in reserve. His recent form suggests he's more than capable of wire-to-wire success when allowed to settle into rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Reshuffle
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate and the race becomes tactical approaching halfway.
scenarios.body: Prominent runners like Sea Invasion and Tommie Beau can position close enough to strike when the tempo lifts approaching the business end. This allows versatile horses to adapt their tactics and stay in contention throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the going rides slower than advertised and becomes a true staying test.
scenarios.body: The extended trip combined with testing ground conditions turns this into an old-fashioned stamina examination where only the most genuine stayers survive. Unanswered Prayers and Planned Paradise have the profiles to excel in these conditions.

watchPoints.text: Rivers Corner could get an uncontested lead if Largy Poet doesn't fire, allowing him to control the race completely
Transmission's 64-day absence could leave him short of peak fitness despite strong work reports
Invincible Nao has home advantage with strong Plumpton record and proven ability at this trip
Largy Poet's headgear change from blinkers back to cheekpieces suggests connections are still searching for the key
Planned Paradise's 12-day turnaround after a hard-fought Hexham win could take its toll in the closing stages

races.name: Gordon And Angela Ashdown Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: A Tickatickatiming
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong course form who should track Public Enemy and benefit from the tactical setup
runners_data.comment: Bumper/maiden hurdle winner here in 2023; in good form and should be close up again
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper and maiden hurdle winner on this course in 2023; has run some good races in defeat here since early last spring and has a chance at the weights with Yasmina on a C&D run in February; improvement not really in the offing but she can be involved.

runners_data.name: Unjeu Royal
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 77-day break with bleeding concerns, faces traffic problems from crowded back division
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner; promising 2m hurdle form; likely to be competitive on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won Southwell bumper in February 2025; bled from the nose at Lingfield in January but has been ready to run since February and an earlier run, a promising runner-up to a useful one at Huntingdon (2m, good to soft) in November, suggests he will be competitive on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Public Enemy
runners_data.note: Lone front runner whose course and distance win gives him tactical control, though handicap form disappointing
runners_data.comment: Won good-ground maiden/novice hurdles last spring but ordinary handicap form so far
runners_data.spotlight: Won good-ground maiden (C&D) and novice hurdles last spring but he ran poorly on handicap debut here in between and his form at this level since hasn't borne much fruit (first-time tongue-tie latest, blinkers now added); however, he may well do better on second run back from a break with Sam Twiston-Davies taking over.

runners_data.name: Risk It All
runners_data.note: Quality hold-up horse whose class could tell if he finds racing room, but faces inevitable traffic problems
runners_data.comment: French Flat winner but proving hard to place over hurdles so far; needs extra
runners_data.spotlight: French Flat winner in 2024; maiden hurdler who is proving hard to place in handicaps, albeit his latest defeat, over C&D last month, came at the hands of one who'd dropped a long way in the weights; needs more.

runners_data.name: Yasmina
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose recent course win over A Tickatickatiming gives confidence, but 56-day absence and crowded closer ranks concern
runners_data.comment: Had wind op before forging clear of A Tickatickatiming on handicap debut over C&D; up 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Hinted at minor ability before having wind surgery and the operation seemed to help as she forged clear of A Tickatickatiming on handicap debut over C&D (soft) in February; should make a go of it off 3lb higher.

runners_data.name: Fascinating Lips
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran whose 146-day break and advancing years make task difficult in competitive handicap
runners_data.comment: Hurdle winner in 2022 but minor form in the autumn and has left the Moores since
runners_data.spotlight: Hurdle winner in 2022 whose latest success came in a classified event (1m2f) last August when with the Moores; minor hurdle form in the autumn and up against it for new yard after a break.

runners_data.name: Galactic Jack
runners_data.note: Bottom weight hold-up horse whose recent poor form and lengthy absence make him hard to fancy despite useful flat ability
runners_data.comment: Useful Flat form in 2023; very mixed since but on lowly mark on 2nd run back from absence
runners_data.spotlight: Useful on the Flat, won 1m4f Salisbury handicap in 2023 off a mark of 88; more off days than on in the meantime but soft ground no help on recent yard debut after nearly two years off; worth a market check off a very low mark now back on more suitable ground; cheekpieces refitted.

races.paceDynamic: Public Enemy is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start, with A Tickatickatiming likely to track him prominently. The pace should be manageable rather than breakneck given the small field and lack of multiple early leaders. Behind this duo, five hold-up horses (Unjeu Royal, Risk It All, Yasmina, Fascinating Lips, Galactic Jack) will be looking to pounce late. This tactical setup strongly favours the prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems and kickback that the crowded pack of hold-up horses will create in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Public Enemy and A Tickatickatiming get first run on the field turning for home
scenarios.body: The front two will have clear sailing while the five hold-up horses get in each other's way behind, creating a tactical nightmare for the back markers. The prominent pair's positional advantage becomes decisive when the cavalry charge arrives too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and one of the closers gets a dream run through
scenarios.body: A single hold-up horse threads the needle perfectly while others remain trapped, capitalizing on Public Enemy and A Tickatickatiming potentially going too slow early. Risk It All or Yasmina most likely to benefit from superior class.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Public Enemy goes too slow and gets swamped by multiple closers in a bunched finish
scenarios.body: The entire field arrives together with positioning and jockeyship becoming crucial in a messy finale. Multiple hold-up horses get competitive but none gets clear daylight to assert properly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Triumph
scenarios.trigger: If Public Enemy gets an uncontested lead and stays on strongly
scenarios.body: A Tickatickatiming fails to provide enough early pressure, allowing Public Enemy to control the race completely and resist all late challenges. His course and distance win gives him the edge in a tactical affair.

watchPoints.text: Public Enemy could get too easy a time in front if A Tickatickatiming doesn't apply enough early pressure
The five hold-up horses Risk It All, Unjeu Royal, Yasmina, Fascinating Lips and Galactic Jack creating a traffic nightmare behind the leaders
A Tickatickatiming's jumping under pressure as he tries to keep tabs on Public Enemy throughout
Yasmina and Risk It All needing significant racing room late given their hold-up styles in this tactical affair
Unjeu Royal's breathing after previous bleeding episode, especially under late pressure

races.name: BetGoodwin Best Odds Guaranteed Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cheap Sandwiches
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who disappointed on heavy ground at Fontwell but returns to suitable conditions with proven ability on good surfaces.
runners_data.comment: Promising second on bumper debut and subsequent lesser run was on heavy ground
runners_data.spotlight: Promising third in sole point and runner-up on bumper debut at Warwick (2m, good to soft) in December; disappointing at Fontwell since but the ground was heavy; retains potential and could bounce back with big run.

runners_data.name: Kamille Au Kanada
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strong point-to-point form on similar going, though the disqualification raises minor questions about connections.
runners_data.comment: First past the post in both points; fourth in Listed mares' bumper last time; player
runners_data.spotlight: First past the post in both Irish points (good to yielding/soft), disqualified on first occasion (banned substance in sample); 14l fourth at 11-1 in Listed mares' bumper at Sandown (2m, soft) on last month's rules debut; her sights are lowered today and she could play a leading role.

runners_data.name: Hitintheheadlines
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 105-day absence but showed tactical pace when third on Ascot debut over shorter trip.
runners_data.comment: A touch underwhelming at Huntingdon last time but he remains one to be interested in
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner who also showed promise when third of six on bumper debut at Ascot (1m7f, good) in November; failed to build on that when fifth of eight at Huntingdon (2m, good to soft) but he's in top hands and remains one to be interested in.

runners_data.name: Mint Approved
runners_data.note: Front-running type who ran well when runner-up over course and distance last month, though others hold stronger overall form.
runners_data.comment: 1-4 in points and runner-up in C&D bumper last month; open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: One win from four point starts and ran well from the front when back in a bumper and runner-up over C&D (good to soft) last month; others have stronger form but he's open to improvement, especially if settling better.

races.paceDynamic: Cheap Sandwiches and Mint Approved both show prominent tendencies and will likely share early pace-making duties over this 2m2f trip. With only four runners, the pace should be sustainable rather than frantic, allowing the race to develop into a tactical affair. Kamille Au Kanada and Hitintheheadlines as hold-up horses will rely on the prominent pair maintaining enough gallop to set up their finishing kicks. This honest but not searingly fast tempo clearly favours horses who can settle and deliver a late burst rather than those forced to do the donkey work.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pair maintain a steady but undemanding gallop through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect tactical scenario with plenty left in the tank for their trademark finishing kicks. Kamille Au Kanada's point-to-point success and Hitintheheadlines' tactical speed become decisive assets.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Running Success
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent pair steals a march and the hold-up horses are caught napping
scenarios.body: The tactical runners find themselves with too much ground to make up in the closing stages as the early pace proves more testing than anticipated. Cheap Sandwiches or Mint Approved benefit from getting first run on their rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Battle
scenarios.trigger: If all four stay within striking distance entering the final half-mile creating a genuine four-way fight
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of raw ability and stamina rather than tactics, with form lines and ratings proving most reliable. The highest-rated performers with proven stamina reserves edge clear in a thrilling finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both prominent runners go too fast early and tie up dramatically in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses benefit from an unsustainable early gallop that plays perfectly into their hands. Even moderate finishing kicks prove sufficient to reel in the exhausted pace-setters.

watchPoints.text: Kamille Au Kanada drops in significantly behind the early pace-setters as her hold-up style requires a strong gallop to be effective
Cheap Sandwiches shows early keen tendencies given the 43-day break and gets involved in an unnecessary pace battle
Hitintheheadlines shows signs of rustiness in the early stages after the extended 105-day layoff
Mint Approved attempts to make all the running but lacks company up front and sets unsustainable fractions
The pace becomes overly steady through the middle sections, negating the hold-up horses' tactical advantages
